question: The physical quantity having a unit of volt/ampere is __________.
solution:
The **correct** answer is__ **resistance**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ohm **is the **SI unit **for measuring **resistance**.
 
• The **volt** per** amp** represents the **ohm.**
 
• The name was derived from **George Ohm,** a **German physicist**.
 
• **Resistance** is the degree to which a substance **obstructs** or opposes an **electric current**.
 
• **Electron flow **is referred to as electric **current**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Facts about **Charge**:

 
 
• The **coulomb **is a derived **SI unit** that is used to measure **electric charge**. 
 
• It is **denoted** by the letter **C**.
 
• **One ampere** per second of **electrical current** across a wire is **equal** to one **coulomb **of charge.
 
• Protons and **electrons** are the two main charge carriers for both** positive **and **negative** electric **charges**.
 
 
 
• **Facts** about** Work**:
 
 
• The **quantity** of energy that is** transmitted** from **one form **or item to another is referred to as the **work.**
 
• **Transferring** that energy is what it means to **work**.
 
• A **force** must be applied over a **distance** in order to **perform **work.
 
• Energy transfer into or out of a thing** depends** on the sign of the **work performed** on it.
 
 
 
• Facts about **Current**:
 
 
• An **electrical** charge carrier flow known as **current often** involves **electrons** or atoms lacking in electrons.
 
• The **capital letter I** frequently used as a **symbol **for current**. **
 
• **Amperes** are the common unit and are denoted by the letter **A**.
 
• Essentially, **electric current** is the flow or charge of an **electric charge** that is in motion in a **conductor**.
 
• There must be a net flow of charge through the area for it to be present.
 
• I=**timecharge** is a formula that **expresses** the current as the charge flow **per second.**
 
• **Ampere** is the name of the **current SI unit**.
